titleEn: Break It in Half—Yum for Two!

pages.text: "The last crescent bread!" Coco, a little mouse in a red headscarf, took the only loaf left on the shelf. It was afternoon, and every other shelf was empty. "Mine! I won't share even a bite!"
Jingle! Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, came in. His eyebrows drooped at the empty shelves. Coco hugged the bread to their chest and turned away. "I won't give you any!"
In a corner, Coco bit into the bread. But however much Coco chewed, it had no flavor. "Huh? Why doesn't it taste good?" Grandpa sat on a chair, empty-handed.
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, sat beside Coco. "You have a whole loaf. Why the sad mouth?" Coco glanced at Grandpa. "...Because Grandpa has nothing."
Mom smiled. "Bread tastes better shared. Break it in half, and there's yum for two." Coco looked down at the bread in their paws. "Break it in half—yum for two?"
Coco held the bread in both paws and broke it in half. Steam drifted from the broken middle. Two matching pieces of crescent bread.
Coco hurried to Grandpa with one piece. "Grandpa, half is yours!" His smile reached his ears. "Thank you, Coco."
Side by side, they ate the crescent bread. Yum, yum! The flavor missing before now filled Coco's mouth. Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. "Eating together brought the taste back!"
Now Coco knew how to share. "One, look beside me! Two, break it in half! Three, yum for two!" At snack time the next day, Coco broke a cookie at the dough table and held out half.
Mom hugged Coco softly. "Those paws that offer half have grown up!" Bread broken in half tastes better than a whole loaf eaten alone. Coco called, "Break it in half—yum for two!"
